column1: # The published Samoan scriptures use the older unmarked orthography, so the
# bundled text carries almost no macrons (ā ē ī ō ū) or glottal stops. This
# table restores them, one WORD TYPE at a time, so the app can offer a marked
# reading register for learners without altering the official text.
#   form   = normalized lowercase core (no leading/trailing punctuation)
#   marked = the same word with diacritics restored
#   note   = optional; prefix "?" if the entry still needs a native check
# Rows where marked == form are "reviewed, no change needed" — they record that
# a human looked at the word, which is why they're worth keeping.
# GLOTTAL STOP is written U+2019 (’) to match the existing text, which already
# spells a’u / o’u / lo’u that way. Do not introduce U+02BB (ʻ) here.
# WORD-INITIAL GLOTTALS ARE NOT WRITTEN in this edition — only intra-word ones.
# `aai` becomes `a’ai`, marking the intra-word glottal while leaving the initial
# one bare. This matches the source, which marks a’u / lo’u / o’u and nothing
# word-initial. Consequence: lexical pairs distinguished only by an initial
# glottal (au "current" vs ’au "company") are simply not distinguished here.
# Ordered by corpus frequency, most common first. Coverage after each batch is
